parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Design intent: V-001, a three-phase FWKO, separates well fluid into gas, oil and free water by density at nominal 60 psig/130 °F. Gas leaves under PV-101 pressure control to fuel gas, with excess to the burn pit. Oil leaves under level control to the Heater-Treater and then V-003. Water leaves under level control to water treatment. E-001 is associated equipment, but its position and duty are not stated. The guidewords No/Less/More/Reverse/Another/Fire-Explosion/Error were applied to all six source-study elements across the inlet, gas, oil and water boundaries. Highest-priority hazards: (1) V-001 overpressure from a blocked gas outlet, surge, overfill, fire or start-up line-up error, where the final safeguard PSV-101 A/B has unverified set pressure and sizing; (2) gas blow-by through the liquid outlets to Heater-Treater or water treatment equipment that may be rated lower; (3) liquid carryover to fuel gas and the burn pit; and (4) fire/explosion from loss of containment. Medium items include common-cause valve failure, corrosion/erosion, reverse flow, interface upsets affecting Heater-Treater/V-003, E-001 leakage and temperature deviations. Listed safeguards are mainly basic control loops plus PSVs and SDVs whose trip functions are not stated. Recommendations therefore focus on: reconciling P/T data; verifying relief cases; confirming or adding independent high/low level and high-pressure trips on the SDVs; documenting fail positions; corrosion/solids management; and a formal start-up line-up procedure. Risk classes are qualitative and for prioritisation only.
